hints.title: Look at the end
hints.body: A valid chunking of a prefix ends with either the final digit alone or the final two digits together. Count the ways those two possibilities contribute.

hints.title: Prefix state
hints.body: Let `ways[i]` be the number of valid chunkings of the first `i` digits. The answer is `ways[n]`, and `ways[0]` is `1` because the empty prefix has one trivial chunking.

hints.title: Respect zeros
hints.body: A single final digit can be used only when it is not `0`. A final pair can be used only when it forms a number from `10` through `26`, which means its first digit is `1`, or it is `2` followed by `0` through `6`.

hints.title: Pseudocode
hints.body:
```
twoBack = 1
oneBack = (digits[0] != '0') ? 1 : 0
for i from 1 to length(digits) - 1:
    current = 0
    if digits[i] != '0':
        current += oneBack
    if digits[i-1] == '1' or (digits[i-1] == '2' and digits[i] <= '6'):
        current += twoBack
    twoBack = oneBack
    oneBack = current
return oneBack
```

This is pseudocode, not a complete solution.
